Package io.github.janglada.orkit.scheduling

package io.github.janglada.orkit.scheduling
Employee shift-scheduling solver.

Defines a fluent DSL for modeling weekly or multi-week rosters: employees, shifts (day/evening/night with start/end times), hard constraints (Rules) and soft objectives (Goals).

Shifts may require several skills and a role mix; employees may have weekly maximum, minimum and contracted hours. The roster reports each assignment's role and cost, the total labor cost in currency, and each employee's hours.

Entry point: Optimize.scheduling().

    Hard constraint applied to the scheduling model.
    Rule.ForbidSequence
    Forbids an employee from working a shift of toCategory on the calendar day right after a shift of fromCategory, whatever the clock times.
    Rule.MaxConsecutiveNightShifts
    At most maxNights night shifts in any run of maxNights + 1 consecutive calendar days per employee.
    Rule.MaxConsecutiveWorkDays
    Caps the number of consecutive calendar days an employee may work.
    Rule.MaxShiftsPerWeek
    At most maxShifts assignments in any rolling 7-day window per employee.
    Rule.MinRestBetweenShifts
    Minimum rest gap that must separate any two shifts worked by the same employee.
    Rule.OneShiftPerEmployeePerDay
    Forbids an employee from being assigned to more than one shift on any single calendar day.

    Fluent configurator for a shift, used inside the lambda passed to SchedulingBuilder.shift(String, java.util.function.Consumer).
    SoftGoal
    Soft preference folded into the weighted objective.
    SoftGoal.BalanceWorkloadAcrossEmployees
    Penalize the spread between the most- and least-loaded employee.
    SoftGoal.HonorEmployeePreferences
    Reward (subtract from the objective) each satisfied employee shift preference.
    SoftGoal.PenalizeContractDeviation
    Penalize every minute an employee works above or below their contracted hours in a full week.
    SoftGoal.PenalizeUnderstaffing
    Penalize each employee missing between a shift's minimum and its target.
